Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: A common fungal disease of apple trees that thrives in cool, wet spring weather. It can significantly reduce fruit quality and yield if left untreated.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungal infection caused by Venturia inaequalis. Spreads in wet and cool weather conditions.
symptoms: Dark olive-green spots on leaves and fruits.
Leaves may curl and fall early.
Infected fruits develop dark, scabby lesions.
Severe infections cause premature leaf drop.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits immediately.
Apply fungicide spray (Mancozeb or Captan) every 7-10 days during wet season.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: A serious fungal disease that affects fruits, leaves, and bark of apple trees. It can cause significant crop losses if not managed early.
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Enters through wounds or dead wood.
symptoms: Brown to black circular spots on fruits.
Leaves show purple spots with brown centers.
Infected fruits shrivel and turn black.
Cankers may form on branches.
treatment: Prune and destroy all dead or infected branches.
Apply copper-based fungicide during early growing season.
Remove mummified fruits from trees and ground.
Keep orchard clean of plant debris.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease that requires both apple and cedar/juniper trees to complete its life cycle. Common in areas where both tree types grow nearby.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae requiring both apple and cedar trees.
symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface.
Small tube-like structures on lower leaf.
Leaves may yellow and drop early.
Fruits may develop deformed areas.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Myclobutanil) from pink bud stage through summer.
Remove nearby cedar or juniper trees if possible.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties for future planting.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple
Apple___healthy.description: No disease detected. The plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.

Blueberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The blueberry plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.

No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.

Maintain acidic soil pH between 4.5 and 5.5.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry Powdery Mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that appears as white powdery growth on cherry leaves and shoots. It thrives in warm days and cool nights with high humidity.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungal infection caused by Podosphaera clandestina. Favored by warm days and cool nights.
symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves and shoots.
Infected leaves curl and distort.
Shoot growth may be stunted.
Severely infected leaves may turn yellow and drop.
treatment: Apply sulfur-based fungicide at first sign of infection.
Prune infected shoots to reduce spread.
Improve air circulation through proper pruning.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.name: Healthy Cherry
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: No disease detected. The cherry plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain good orchard hygiene.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: One of the most significant fungal diseases of corn worldwide. It thrives in warm, humid conditions and can cause severe yield loss.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. Common in humid conditions.
symptoms: Rectangular gray to tan lesions on leaves.
Lesions run parallel to leaf veins.
Lesions may merge causing large dead areas.
Severe infection leads to premature plant death.
treatment: Plant resistant corn varieties.
Apply fungicide (Azoxystrobin) at early sign of infection.
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops.
Till crop residue after harvest to reduce fungal survival.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A widespread fungal disease that spreads rapidly through wind-blown spores. Most damaging during cool, moist weather conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi. Spreads through wind-blown spores.
symptoms: Small oval brick-red pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Pustules may turn dark brown as they mature.
Heavily infected leaves turn yellow and die.
Infection is more severe on young plants.
treatment: Plant rust-resistant hybrid varieties.
Apply fungicide spray if infection is severe before tasseling.
Scout fields regularly during cool and humid weather.
Early planting can help avoid peak rust season.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A serious foliar disease of corn that can cause yield losses of 30-50% in severe cases. Spreads quickly under moderate temperatures and wet conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Favored by moderate temperatures and wet weather.
symptoms: Long elliptical gray-green to tan lesions on leaves.
Lesions can reach 2.5 to 15 cm in length.
Lesions may have dark borders.
Severe infection causes significant yield loss.
treatment: Plant resistant hybrid varieties.
Apply fungicide at early tasseling stage.
Rotate crops to break disease cycle.
Deep till infected crop residue after harvest.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy Corn
Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: No disease detected. The plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No lesions, spots, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain proper spacing for air circulation.

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape Black Rot
Grape___Black_rot.description: A devastating fungal disease of grapes that can destroy entire crops. Warm, wet weather during early growing season significantly increases severity.
Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Guignardia bidwellii. Spreads in warm and wet conditions.
symptoms: Small yellow spots on leaves that turn brown with dark borders.
Infected berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
Black lesions appear on stems and tendrils.
Entire clusters can be destroyed in severe infections.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Myclobutanil) from bud break through berry set.
Remove and destroy mummified berries and infected leaves.
Prune vines to improve air circulation.
Practice good vineyard sanitation throughout the season.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Grape Esca (Black Measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex fungal disease also known as Black Measles. It is a chronic vine disease that can persist for years and gradually weaken or kill the vine.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Complex fungal disease caused by multiple fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora.
symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellow and brown on leaves.
Berries develop dark spots giving a measles-like appearance.
Internal wood shows dark streaking when cut.
Sudden vine collapse can occur in severe cases.
treatment: Prune out and destroy infected wood.
Protect pruning wounds with fungicide paste.
Avoid large pruning wounds during wet weather.
Remove severely infected vines to protect surrounding plants.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Grape Leaf Blight
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal leaf disease of grapes that causes significant defoliation in warm and humid conditions. Mainly affects leaves rather than fruits.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungal infection caused by Isariopsis clavispora (Pseudocercospora vitis).
symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on upper leaf surface.
Spots enlarge and merge causing large dead areas.
Severe infection leads to premature defoliation.
Weakens vines and reduces next season yield.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Copper oxychloride) at early sign.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Ensure proper vine spacing for air circulation.
Avoid excessive irrigation that increases humidity.

Grape___healthy.name: Healthy Grape
Grape___healthy.description: No disease detected. The grape vine appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain proper vine training and pruning.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus Greening (Huanglongbing)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: One of the most serious citrus diseases in the world with no known cure. It is spread by a tiny insect and can kill a citrus tree within a few years of infection.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterial disease caused by Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus. Spread by Asian citrus psyllid insect.
symptoms: Yellow mottling of leaves — asymmetric blotchy yellowing.
Fruits remain small, lopsided, and bitter.
Fruits may stay green at the bottom even when ripe.
Tree gradually declines and dies over several years.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected trees immediately to prevent spread.
Control Asian citrus psyllid with insecticide sprays.
Use certified disease-free planting material.
There is no cure — prevention and vector control are critical.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach Bacterial Spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A common and destructive bacterial disease of peaches and nectarines. Warm, wet, and windy conditions favor its spread and severity.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni. Spread by wind and rain.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow margins.
Spots may fall out leaving a shot-hole appearance.
Fruits develop small pits and cracks with dark spots.
Severe infections cause defoliation and reduced fruit quality.
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide in early spring before symptoms appear.
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness.
Plant resistant peach varieties where available.
Remove and destroy severely infected plant material.

Peach___healthy.name: Healthy Peach
Peach___healthy.description: No disease detected. The peach tree appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain good orchard hygiene.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A serious bacterial disease affecting bell peppers in warm, wet conditions. It affects leaves, stems, and fruits and can cause severe yield loss.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria. Spread by rain and contaminated tools.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halos.
Spots may coalesce causing large dead areas.
Fruits develop raised, scabby, dark lesions.
Severe infections cause premature defoliation.
treatment: Use certified disease-free seeds and transplants.
Apply copper-based bactericide spray every 5-7 days during wet weather.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Remove and destroy infected plant material immediately.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Healthy Bell Pepper
Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: No disease detected. The bell pepper plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering at soil level.
Apply balanced fertilizer as needed.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease of potatoes that typically affects older leaves first. Warm temperatures and high humidity favor disease development.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Favored by warm temperatures and high humidity.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves.
Yellow area surrounding the spots.
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
Severe infection moves upward to younger leaves.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil) at first sign of disease.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Practice crop rotation — do not plant potatoes in same field consecutively.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: One of the most devastating plant diseases in history — responsible for the Irish Potato Famine. Can destroy an entire crop within days under cool, wet conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool and wet conditions.
symptoms: Large irregular dark water-soaked patches on leaves.
White mold visible on leaf undersides in humid weather.
Infected tubers develop dark, firm rot.
Plants may collapse entirely within days in severe cases.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Metalaxyl or Mancozeb) immediately at first sign.
Remove and destroy all infected plant parts.
Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation.
Use certified disease-free seed potatoes.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato
Potato___healthy.description: No disease detected. The potato plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.

treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.

Raspberry___healthy.name: Healthy Raspberry
Raspberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The raspberry plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.

treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.

Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.name: Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.description: A serious bacterial disease of rice caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, leading to wilting and yellowing of leaves. One of the most devastating rice diseases in Asia.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.cause: Bacterial infection caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. Spreads through infected water, rain splash, and wounds.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions along leaf margins turning yellow.
Yellowing and wilting of leaves from the tip downward.
Milky or opaque bacterial ooze visible on lesions in the morning.
Entire leaf may dry out in severe cases.
treatment: Use copper-based bactericides at early infection stage.
Apply streptomycin-based sprays if available.
Remove and destroy heavily infected plant material.
Drain fields and avoid flood irrigation during outbreaks.

Rice___Brown_Spot.name: Rice Brown Spot
Rice___Brown_Spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Cochliobolus miyabeanus that affects rice leaves and grains. Historically associated with the 1943 Bengal famine. Reduces yield significantly.
Rice___Brown_Spot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Cochliobolus miyabeanus. Favored by nutrient-deficient soils.
symptoms: Oval to circular brown spots on leaves with grey or whitish centers.
Dark brown borders surrounding the spots.
Spots also appear on glumes and grains causing discoloration.
Severely infected leaves turn yellow and dry out.
treatment: Apply fungicides like Iprodione or Tricyclazole at first sign.
Use potassium silicate to strengthen plant cell walls.
Improve soil fertility especially potassium and phosphorus.

Rice___Healthy.name: Healthy Rice
Rice___Healthy.description: No disease detected. The rice plant appears to be in good health with green upright leaves and no visible lesions or discoloration.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green, upright, and free from lesions.
No spots, discoloration, or wilting visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain proper field drainage.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.name: Rice Leaf Blast
Rice___Leaf_Blast.description: One of the most destructive rice diseases worldwide caused by Magnaporthe oryzae fungus. Can cause complete crop failure under favorable conditions.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.cause: Fungal infection caused by Magnaporthe oryzae. Spreads through wind-blown spores in humid conditions.
symptoms: Diamond or eye-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown borders on leaves.
White to gray spindle-shaped spots on young leaves.
Rapid leaf blighting and browning in severe cases.
Collar rot at the base of leaves in neck blast stage.
treatment: Apply Tricyclazole or Isoprothiolane fungicides at early infection.
Use silicon fertilizers to strengthen plant cell walls.
Apply fungicide at booting stage to prevent neck blast.

Rice___Leaf_Scald.name: Rice Leaf Scald
Rice___Leaf_Scald.description: A fungal disease caused by Microdochium oryzae that produces a characteristic scalded appearance on rice leaves. Common in tropical and subtropical regions.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.cause: Fungal infection caused by Microdochium oryzae. Favored by high humidity and dense planting.
symptoms: Irregular lesions with light tan or straw-colored centers on leaves.
Zonate or banded appearance giving a scalded look.
Lesions have dark brown margins.
Affected leaves dry out from the tip downward.
treatment: Apply appropriate fungicides at early infection stage.
Remove and destroy heavily infected plant debris.
Improve field drainage to reduce humidity.

Rice___Sheath_Blight.name: Rice Sheath Blight
Rice___Sheath_Blight.description: A major rice disease caused by Rhizoctonia solani fungus. Particularly severe under high humidity and dense planting. One of the most economically important rice diseases globally.
Rice___Sheath_Blight.cause: Fungal infection caused by Rhizoctonia solani. Survives in soil and spreads through water and infected debris.
symptoms: Oval or elliptical lesions on leaf sheaths near water level.
Lesions have gray-white centers with dark brown borders.
Lesions spread upward to higher sheaths and leaves.
Lodging of plants in severe infections.
treatment: Apply fungicides like Validamycin or Hexaconazole at early stage.
Use biological control agents like Trichoderma harzianum.
Drain fields periodically to reduce humidity.

Soybean___healthy.name: Healthy Soybean
Soybean___healthy.description: No disease detected. The soybean plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash Powdery Mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A very common fungal disease of squash and other cucurbits. Unlike most fungal diseases, it thrives in warm dry conditions with low humidity.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungal infection caused by Podosphaera xanthii. Thrives in warm, dry conditions.
symptoms: White powdery spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Spots enlarge to cover entire leaf surface.
Infected leaves turn yellow then brown and die.
Severe infection reduces fruit size and quality.
treatment: Apply sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate fungicide at first sign.
Remove severely infected leaves.
Improve air circulation by proper plant spacing.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A common fungal disease of strawberries that causes purplish spots on leaves. Severe infections can reduce plant vigor and fruit yield significantly.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Fungal infection caused by Diplocarpon earlianum. Favored by warm, wet conditions.
symptoms: Small dark purple to red spots on upper leaf surface.
Spots lack a defined border unlike other leaf diseases.
Severely infected leaves turn brown and dry out.
Plant vigor and yield are reduced in chronic infections.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Captan or Myclobutanil) at first sign of infection.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Plant resistant strawberry varieties where available.

Strawberry___healthy.name: Healthy Strawberry
Strawberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The strawberry plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Leaves are green and intact.
No spots, lesions, or discoloration visible.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Remove old leaves and runners as needed.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A highly destructive bacterial disease affecting tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. It spreads rapidly under warm, wet conditions and can devastate crops.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria. Spreads through rain splash and infected seeds.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow margins.
Spots on fruits appear raised and scabby.
Infected leaves may drop prematurely.
Stem lesions may appear dark and water-soaked.
treatment: Use certified disease-free seeds.
Apply copper-based bactericide spray every 7 days.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Remove and destroy infected plant material immediately.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: One of the most common tomato diseases worldwide. It typically starts on older lower leaves and moves upward. Warm humid conditions accelerate its spread.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Common in warm and humid conditions.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves.
Yellow area surrounding spots.
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop.
Dark lesions may also appear on stems and fruits.
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves immediately.
Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil) every 7-10 days.
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash.
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: One of the most devastating tomato diseases, responsible for the Irish Potato Famine. Spreads extremely rapidly in cool, wet weather and can destroy an entire crop within days.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool and wet conditions.
symptoms: Large irregular dark brown patches on leaves.
White mold visible on leaf undersides in humid weather.
Infected fruits develop firm dark brown lesions.
Plants may collapse entirely within days in severe cases.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Metalaxyl or Mancozeb) immediately at first sign.
Remove and destroy all infected plant parts.
Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation.
Destroy crop residue after harvest completely.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease that primarily affects tomatoes grown in greenhouses or high-humidity environments. It rarely affects fruits but can cause significant defoliation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungal infection caused by Passalora fulva. Thrives in high humidity above 85%.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface.
Olive-green to gray velvety mold on leaf undersides.
Infected leaves curl upward and drop.
Severe infections cause significant defoliation.
treatment: Reduce humidity by improving greenhouse ventilation.
Apply fungicide (Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb) at first sign.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: One of the most destructive diseases of tomato foliage. It typically appears after plants begin bearing fruit and spreads rapidly in warm, wet conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici. Spreads through rain splash and infected debris.
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and light gray centers on leaves.
Tiny black dots (fungal bodies) visible in spot centers.
Infected leaves turn yellow then brown and drop.
Disease moves upward from older to younger leaves.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil) at first sign of disease.
Remove infected lower leaves immediately.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Mulch soil to prevent rain splash from soil to leaves.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato Spider Mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Spider mites are tiny pests that suck sap from tomato leaves. They thrive in hot, dry conditions and can rapidly colonize entire plants.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Infestation by Tetranychus urticae (two-spotted spider mite). Thrives in hot, dry weather.
symptoms: Tiny yellow or white stippling dots on upper leaf surface.
Fine webbing on leaves and stems in severe infestations.
Leaves turn bronze, yellow, then brown and drop.
Visible tiny moving dots on leaf undersides.
treatment: Apply miticide or insecticidal soap spray on leaf undersides.
Spray plants with strong water jet to dislodge mites.
Introduce natural predators like predatory mites.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which promotes mite outbreaks.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease that produces distinctive target-like lesions on tomato leaves, stems, and fruits. Warm, humid conditions with frequent rainfall favor its development.
Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Corynespora cassiicola. Favored by warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings forming a target pattern.
Spots appear on leaves, stems, and fruits.
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop.
Fruit lesions are dark, sunken, and may have concentric rings.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Azoxystrobin or Chlorothalonil) at first sign.
Remove and destroy infected plant parts.
Improve air circulation through proper staking and pruning.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A devastating viral disease spread by whiteflies. It is one of the most damaging tomato viruses worldwide, causing severe yield loss with no chemical cure.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Viral disease caused by Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV). Transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci.
symptoms: Leaves curl upward and inward with yellow edges.
Leaves become small, thick, and leathery.
Infected plants are stunted with reduced fruit set.
Flowers may drop without producing fruit.
treatment: Control whitefly population with insecticide or yellow sticky traps.
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies.
Plant virus-resistant tomato varieties.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly contagious viral disease that spreads easily through contact, tools, and hands. It can persist in soil and plant debris for years.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Caused by Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV). Spreads through contact, infected tools, and contaminated hands.
symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves.
Leaves may be distorted, curled, or fern-like.
Fruits may show yellow mottling or uneven ripening.
Plant growth is stunted in severe infections.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Disinfect all tools with bleach solution before use.
Wash hands thoroughly before handling plants.
Plant virus-resistant tomato varieties.

Tomato___healthy.description: No disease detected. The plant appears to be in good health.
symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
